basis: Partner-carried (Erik 2026-09-17 partner-carried rule; decisions.md D3): Box is on the firm's live list only, never on the kpcb.com archive, with a 2007 year; the one KP-side trace is Mamoon Hamid as a director on Box's 2009-2011 Form Ds, when he was at U.S. Venture Partners (he joined Kleiner Perkins in 2017), and Box's 2014 S-1 names no Kleiner Perkins entity among its holders or its financings.

Partner-carried (Erik 2026-09-17 partner-carried rule; decisions.md D3): the firm's card dates a Growth entry to 2021, two years before Leigh Marie Braswell joined; the firm's welcome post of 2023-05-24 lists Chronosphere among the investments she led 'in her first few years in venture', before Kleiner Perkins, and no Kleiner Perkins fund appears in the rounds the Greylock, GV, Lux and Spark rows record.

Ciena listed on Nasdaq in February 1997, before the firm's 1998 year, and no pre-IPO Kleiner Perkins round is on record (T3). The firm's link is ONI Systems, a KP-backed optical company Ciena bought for stock in 2002 (Ciena's 2003 10-Q names KPCB as a defendant in the ONI Systems IPO litigation): the Ciena shares are sale consideration (Erik 2026-09-22), and ONI Systems is the company to add as its own row.

note: Interactive challenges and rewards for game livestreams. BlockchainGamer: 'Azarus has managed to successfully raise more than $1.8m in seed funding' from Galaxy Digital, SVK Crypto, Kleiner Perkins and others (June 2019, the firm's own post the same month). Animoca Brands later took majority ownership, making it a subsidiary (Brave New Coin interview with the CEO), so acquired; its own domain now redirects to a video. No source places its city; country US at low confidence. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

funding_rounds.lead: Galaxy Digital, Animoca Brands, Kleiner Perkins

note: Digital dental and benefits insurance (Beam Benefits), Columbus, Ohio. Its site's footer now names its insurance and administration entities 'wholly owned subsidiaries of Principal Financial Group' (checked 2026-09-30), so acquired. The firm labels a 2018 Growth entry; no source read names the round.

Formally verified hypervisor and security platform; bedrocksystems.com now redirects to BlueRock Security Inc., which operates under that name (checked 2026-09-30): renamed, still private. City Boston from model knowledge, medium. The firm's since-year is 2020; no source read names the round.

Digital mortgage lender, New York; listed on Nasdaq as Better Home & Finance (BETR) since the 2023 SPAC merger, market cap $208.98M on 2026-09-30 (stockanalysis). The firm labels a 2016 Growth entry; no source read names the round.

OKR and performance management software founded by Kris Duggan, Redwood City, with John Doerr on the deal; still private. The firm's since-year is 2013; no source read names the round. Not the Santa Monica BetterWorks (employee perks) of the Redpoint book, a different company.

Plant-based meat, headquartered in El Segundo (Wikipedia). The firm's post of 2019-05-02: 'Kleiner Perkins was the only institutional investor in the first financing round in Beyond Meat back in 2011'; the 2018 S-1 shows that first preferred series was the Series A (5,000,000 shares, $2.0M). The pre-filled 2015 date is a later Form D, so the entry date is 2011.

Blockchain node infrastructure, New York; Coinbase bought it in 2021 (the firm's exit line). The firm's post of 2019-11-19: 'We're excited to welcome Bison Trails to the Kleiner Perkins family and be part of their Series A.'
Bitmoji and comic-avatar maker, Toronto (the pre-filled CA is confirmed); Snap bought it in 2016 (the firm's exit line). The firm labels a 2014 Growth entry; no source read names the round.

Solid oxide fuel cells, San Jose (NYSE: BE). The 2016 draft S-1: 'In 2002, Kleiner Perkins Caufield Byers became our first venture capital investor', without a round name. The pre-filled $3.9B public float is stale: market cap $82.91B on 2026-09-30 (stockanalysis), aligned with the NEA row, so 10b_plus.

Distributed mini-refineries recovering metals from electronic waste (BlueOak Resources; plant in Osceola, Arkansas). Its only Form D gives an investor's Sand Hill Road address, so no source read places the head office, and no acquisition, shutdown or later round was found. Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Mobile location games (MyTown), an iFund company; its first Form D gives the company's address as care of Kleiner Perkins. Palo Alto on the firm's 2008-11 listing; wound down, as the Accel row. The $20M round of 2010 is four times the 2009 entry and graduates the Form D Seed entry (the layer agrees); the Accel row notes Kleiner did the earlier round.

funding_rounds.round: unnamed (Form D; the Accel row reads it Series B)

note: Wearable ventilation for respiratory patients, Irvine, California (its 2017 Form D); Hillrom bought it in 2019 (the firm's exit line). The firm's since-year is 2008 (Fremont on the 2008-11 listing), so the 2014 Form D is a later round and the date is replaced by 2008; no round is named.

Corporate cards and spend management, San Francisco. Wikipedia: the $100M Series C-2 of June 2019 at $2.6B 'was led by Kleiner Perkins', the firm's 2019 Growth entry. Capital One completed its $5.15B acquisition in April 2026, aligned with the IVP, Ribbit, TCV, Tiger and YC rows.

Headless browsers for AI agents, San Francisco. The firm's post of 2024-11-01: 'Browserbase announced its Series A financing, co-led by Kleiner Perkins. This comes after we led their Seed earlier this year', a Seed entry that graduated. Momentum check 2026-09-30: the latest priced round is the $40M Series B of 2025-06-18 led by Notable Capital with Kleiner Perkins (the company's post; press put it at $300M post-money); no $1B+ round found.

Mobile continuous integration and crash reporting, Vancouver; Apple bought it in January 2018 (the firm's exit line), as the First Round row. The firm's since-year is 2016; no source read names the round.

The Bun JavaScript runtime (company Oven), San Francisco. The company's post of 2025-12-02: 'We raised a $7 million seed round led by Kleiner Perkins' and then 'a $19 million Series A led by Khosla Ventures'; the same post announces Bun joining Anthropic (the firm's post 'we proudly led Bun (then called Oven's) Seed').

E-business configuration software, San Jose; IPO 1999, then Chapter 11 in 2001 with its business sold to PeopleSoft: acquired, an asset sale out of insolvency. KPCB held 11.4% in 2001 (its proxy); no round is named.

Endpoint security (incorporated 2002 as Bit9, renamed after buying Carbon Black in 2014), Waltham, Massachusetts; IPO 2018, bought by VMware in 2019. The 2018 S-1 has KPCB XII (a 2006 fund) holding 8.8% and buying Series F; the firm's since-year is 2006, and no source read names the round it first joined.

Microcatheters for electrophysiology, Fremont. The 1997 prospectus lists Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers VI buying 285,714 Series A shares (then C, D and E), with Joe Lacob chairman from May 1993. Defunct after its 2010 bankruptcy decision, aligned with the NEA row.

Gene-expression tests for coronary artery disease, Palo Alto (the 2013 S-1). Incorporated July 2003 with Brook Byers a director from July 2003 and its CEO until August 2004, so Kleiner Perkins was there at formation and the 2010 Form D band (Growth) is a follow-on; the founding round is not named. The IPO was withdrawn, filings stop in 2017 and its domain now serves an unrelated site (checked 2026-09-30): defunct, medium confidence.
Transplant diagnostics (formerly XDx), Brisbane, California (Nasdaq: CDNA).

Synthetic-biology cell therapy from Wendell Lim's UCSF lab; Kite Pharma (Gilead) bought it in 2017 (the firm's exit line: Gilead Sciences). City San Francisco from knowledge; the 2016 Form D gives an officer's Lafayette address.

SONET optical access equipment, Petaluma; Cisco bought it in 1999. Wikipedia: founded in 1997 as Fiberlane Communications 'with funding from Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers and Vinod Khosla as the managing VC'; no round name (the firm's card says 1998).

Phased-array satellite and airborne communications, Austin. Its 2026 Series C ($270M equity plus EXIM debt) disclosed no valuation; press cites only an unnamed source that it crossed $1B, which is no citable figure (Rule A), so below_1b until a priced mark is published (a Series D was under way in August 2026).
EV charging network, Campbell, California (NYSE: CHPT).
AI food-assembly robots, San Francisco. The firm's since-year is 2019; no source read names the round. No $1B+ priced round on record.
Student learning services, Santa Clara (NYSE: CHGG).

Online marketplace for retail electricity and gas plans, San Francisco; Red Ventures bought it (the firm's exit line). The firm labels a 2012 Growth entry (Greentech team); no source read names the round.

Application and desktop virtualization, Fort Lauderdale; IPO 1995, taken private by Vista and Elliott in 2022 and combined with TIBCO. Kevin Compton, a KP general partner from 1990, was a director from 1991 (its 2001 proxy); the firm's since-year is 1989 and no round is named.

Residential solar finance marketplace, San Francisco (222 7th Street on its 2011 Form D); it became Spruce Finance and was bought by XL Fleet in 2022 (now Spruce Power): acquired. A Green Growth Fund position (Ben Kortlang) whose first round is not named in any source read.

Cloud cost management, Boston; VMware bought it in 2018. Wikipedia: 'In June 2017, CloudHealth Technologies secured $46 million in Series D funding led by Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers', the firm's 2017 Growth entry.

Analytics for virtualized data centres, Santa Clara; Hewlett Packard Enterprise bought it in 2018 (the firm's exit line: HPE). The firm's since-year is 2012 (Mike Abbott); no source read names the round.

The coda.io all-in-one doc, Mountain View, as the General Catalyst, Greylock and NEA rows; Grammarly bought it in December 2024. The firm's post of 2020-08-11: 'We're excited to be part of Coda's pursuit of productivity and lead their Series C', its first round in the company (the card's 2014 year predates any KP round on record). Not the Coda Payments of Singapore in the Insight book.

Browser-based development environments, Amsterdam (CodeSandbox, Inc. files its Form D from San Francisco as the US entity, hence the pre-filled US); Together AI bought it in December 2024 (SiliconANGLE), aligned with the EQT Ventures row.
Care-coordination network for high-need patients, Salt Lake City; PointClickCare bought it in 2020 (the firm's exit line). The firm labels a 2017 Growth entry; no source read names the round.
Personal computers, Houston; IPO 1983, bought by HP in 2002. The firm's own card calls it one of its most important bets (1982); no round is named.

AI software organising biopharma information. The firm's post of 2025-08-19: 'We're thrilled to be partnering with Convoke in their seed funding round'; the card's year 2024 is the close year. Neither the company's site nor the post places a city. Graduation left for the graduation pass.
Container Linux and Kubernetes (Tectonic), San Francisco; Red Hat bought it for $250M in January 2018, aligned with the a16z, GV and YC rows.
Application service provider, San Carlos; IPO 2000, bought by IBM in 2005. Ted Schlein a director from September 1998 (its 2002 proxy); the firm's since-year is 1998 and no round is named.
Vaccine adjuvants and immunotherapeutics, Seattle; GlaxoSmithKline bought it in 2005. Joe Lacob was a director from 1994 and chairman to 1999 (its 2001 proxy); no round is named.
Relaxin for acute heart failure, San Mateo (the firm's 2008-11 listing); Novartis bought it in 2010 (the archived page reads Acquired from 2012).
Wireless cardiac monitoring patches, San Jose (the firm's 2008-11 listing); Medtronic bought it in 2014 (the firm's exit line). Founded in 2005, the firm's since-year; no round is named.
